clue.text: Advance across delta by small boat

blocks.note: over means across, as in going over the road
D is delta in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a raft is a small, simple craft

explanation.surface: Troops push forward over a river delta, ferried across on little boats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Advance' reads as a military push, but it is a noun for money lent ahead of time.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank overdraft is credit lent ahead of the money in the account, a kind of loan or advance.

clue.text: Greek character and others one’s assumed nameless

indicators.note: without a name means the letter standing for name must be taken away
to assume is to take on or put on, so one word takes the other inside it

blocks.note: taken as written, losing its N for name
the rest are the others

explanation.surface: A list of Greek figures where everyone has taken on a false identity and dropped their real name.
explanation.walkthrough: N is the standard abbreviation for name; ONE'S without it is OES, which then takes REST inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Orestes, son of Agamemnon, is a figure from Greek myth and tragedy who avenged his murdered father.

clue.text: Magician left without female contrived to be mystifying

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is dropped from the word before it
something contrived is artificially put together, so the letters are arranged anew

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, before it loses its F
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A conjuror who left his female assistant behind put on a baffling show.
explanation.walkthrough: LEFT without F is LET; MAGICIAN plus LET is then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Enigmatical is an older form of enigmatic: puzzling, hard to interpret, like a riddle.

clue.text: Put off find (not mine)

indicators.note: the bracketed not tells us to take a word out of the one just given

blocks.note: to determine is to find out or establish
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is told to put off searching, unless the find is somebody else's.
explanation.walkthrough: DETERMINE with its last four letters, MINE, taken away leaves DETER.
explanation.definitionFit: To deter someone is to discourage them, making them less willing to act.

clue.text: Two equal parts? Not hard at all, with a fodder plant

indicators.note: not, with at all, says every occurrence of a letter must go

blocks.note: two halves make two equal parts
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard
taken as written

explanation.surface: A farmer splits a field into two equal parts and plants an easy fodder crop.
explanation.walkthrough: Both H's go from HALF HALF, leaving ALF ALF, and A is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfalfa, also called lucerne, is a leguminous crop grown widely to feed cattle and horses.

clue.text: Drop of water shortly for plant

indicators.note: shortly here means cut short, so the last letter is lost

blocks.note: a tear is a drop of water from the eye

explanation.surface: A gardener soon gives a little water to a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The tea bush, Camellia sinensis, is the shrub whose leaves are dried for the drink.

clue.text: Maybe US criminals had briefly to be imprisoned

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the word loses its final letter
being imprisoned means being locked inside something else

blocks.note: perps is American slang for perpetrators
taken as written, then cut short

explanation.surface: Perhaps the American villains were going to be locked up after all.
explanation.walkthrough: Perps is American police slang for perpetrators, short for the people who committed a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words express possibility without certainty and work interchangeably as adverbs.

clue.text: City in revolution at first pretty backward, rejecting both sides

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the next word
rejecting both sides means both outermost letters are thrown away

blocks.note: first letter of pretty
retrograde means moving backwards

explanation.walkthrough: RETROGRADE loses its first and last letters to give ETROGRAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Petrograd was the name of St Petersburg during the Russian Revolution of 1917.

clue.text: Live on the edge

blocks.note: re means on or concerning
a side is an edge

explanation.surface: Someone lives a risky life on the edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Live on the edge' is an idiom, but only 'Live' is the definition.

clue.text: First Murderer’s speech: I make peers sick, drinking my soup — and the monarch

indicators.note: sick means unwell or disordered, so the letters are thrown into a new order
something drinking takes other material inside itself

taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: The first murderer is Cain, who killed Abel; asked by God where his brother was, he gave this reply in Genesis 4.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible Cain, the first killer, answers God's question about Abel with these evasive words.

clue.text: Shame about horrible noise in tank

a din is a loud, unpleasant noise

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tank' suggests water, but the Saladin was a British armoured car named after the sultan.
explanation.definitionFit: The Saladin was a six-wheeled British armoured fighting vehicle of the 1950s, loosely a tank.

clue.text: To start with alibi for example is a defence

indicators.note: to start with points to the opening letter of the following word

e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for example
taken as written

clue.text: Coming across page, not fond of Shelley? The exact opposite

clue.text: Maybe young member of family has not got on flight

taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: A flight is a series of stairs between floors, and those individual treads are steps.

clue.text: Distance often affected a proclamation from the French

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

clue.text: Uncomfortable with allies failing to eat meal

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

clue.text: Glass changing hands in this checkout cart

clue.text: Working twenty-four hours? At first no — twelve

blocks.note: taken as written
on means working, as a machine is on

clue.text: Fail to understand why coin toss doesn’t produce result?

annotation.answer: NOT MAKE HEAD OR TAIL OF

blocks.clueFragment: why coin toss doesn’t produce result?
blocks.note: surface reading: a puzzle about a flip of a coin that settles nothing

blocks.clueFragment: why coin toss doesn’t produce result?
blocks.note: setter's reading: a toss is decided by which face of the coin lands up; if neither face shows, there is no result

explanation.surface: Someone cannot work out why flipping a coin gave no answer.
explanation.walkthrough: The two faces of a coin are called heads and tails, so a toss with no outcome literally fails to show either.

clue.text: Put down duke, a powerful ruler, to be unmarried

last letter of very
